answer: Require every agent to stake a small refundable deposit before entering the garden of shared tasks, and tie each identity to a verifiable work history. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust: it may only take low-value jobs, and its stake is slashed if peers flag fake work. Reputation accrues slowly, like nectar gathered flower by flower, so one operator spinning up a thousand fresh identities pays a thousand deposits and earns nothing until each builds history. The cost of a sybil swarm becomes linear in identities, while an honest agent pays once.
